chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

For the believer there are three hours: an hour in which he holds private communion with his Lord, an hour in which he manages his livelihood, and an hour in which he frees himself from work to enjoy what is lawful and pleasant.

key_terms.يُنَاجِي: holds private communion or conversation with

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim balance worship, work, and leisure according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) outlines the ideal division of a believer's daily time into three distinct periods: worship (communion with God), work (securing livelihood), and leisure (enjoying lawful pleasures). This teaching emphasizes balance in life, ensuring that religious duties, worldly responsibilities, and personal enjoyment are all given their due proportion. In Shia scholarly tradition, this tripartite model is often cited to refute ascetic isolation, affirming that engaging in lawful leisure and securing one's livelihood are acts of worship when done with the right intention.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 390. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

The believer’s time has three periods : The period when he is in communion with Allāh; the period when he manages for his livelihood; and the period when he is free to enjoy what is lawful and pleasant.
